parts/io: A transformer block takes T tokens, each a vector of d numbers, and returns T vectors of d numbers. Same shape in and out, so blocks can be stacked.
parts/attn: First the tokens exchange information: layer norm, then multi-head attention, and the result is added back to the input. A residual connection: x plus attention of layer norm of x.
parts/mlp: Then each token is processed on its own: layer norm again, then an MLP, added back the same way.
parts/width: The MLP widens each token to four d numbers, applies a ReLU, and comes back down to d. With d of seven hundred sixty eight, its hidden layer is three thousand and seventy two wide.
flow/x: Follow one token through, with d of two. It enters as one and two.
flow/a: For this token, the attention branch returns zero point five and minus one. Added to the input, that makes one point five and one.
flow/m: The MLP branch, reading the normalized sum, returns minus zero point five and two. Added on, that makes one and three: the block's output.
flow/path: The input runs straight through the adds, and each branch only adds a change, as in a residual block. With the norms at the start of each branch, this is called a pre-norm block.
